title: Symptom-Level Comorbidity Patterns Between Depression and Internet Gaming Disorder Among Adolescents: Evidence from Longitudinal Network Analysis with Gender Considerations
abstract: Adolescence is a period with an increased risk for the co-occurrence of depression and Internet gaming disorder (IGD), yet we still know little about how specific symptoms of these two conditions influence each other over time. In this study, we applied cross-lagged panel network analysis to two-wave data from a community sample of 538 adolescents (Mean age = 12.51 years; 53.7 percent female). Potential gender differences in the network structure were examined. In the overall sample and in both gender groups, depressive symptoms consistently predicted later gaming-related problems, whereas no reverse cross-disorder pathways were retained. In particular, suicidal ideation and psychomotor symptoms emerged as bridge symptoms linking depression and IGD, while sleep problems showed moderate outgoing expected influence in the overall symptom network. While boys and girls showed broadly similar patterns, some differences emerged in how specific symptoms were connected and which symptoms were most influential. These findings clarify the longitudinal symptom-level associations between depression and IGD in adolescents, suggesting that addressing key depressive symptoms may help reduce the risk of later IGD.

title: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, AND STRESS AMONG ADOLESCENTS WITH GAMING ADDICTION AND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS
abstract: Gaming disorder is now formally recognized alongside substance use disorders, yet few studies compare the emotional distress associated with the two conditions directly. This study compared depression, anxiety, and stress severity in 400 adolescents, 200 with gaming addiction (GA) and 200 with a substance use disorder (SUD). Participants completed the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales–21 (DASS-21); subscale scores were doubled according to Lovibond and Lovibond (1995) and classified into the five standard severity bands. Pearson chi-square tests showed that the severity distributions differed significantly between groups for depression, χ²(4, N = 400) = 10.12, p = .039, Cramér’s V = .16; anxiety, χ²(4, N = 400) = 24.55, p < .001, V = .25; and stress, χ²(4, N = 400) = 12.71, p = .013, V = .18. In every domain the GA group had a larger share of severe or extremely severe scores (depression 40.5% vs. 27.5%; anxiety 63.0% vs. 41.0%; stress 31.5% vs. 17.0%). Differences were largest for anxiety. Because the design is cross-sectional, causal direction cannot be inferred, but the findings suggest that emotional screening is warranted in gaming addiction.

title: Trauma and problematic gaming: A scoping review of psychological mechanisms and clinical applications
abstract: A substantial body of research indicates that PTSD is associated with elevated risk of addiction. Despite these established patterns in substance use disorders and addictive behaviours, few studies have examined whether comparable mechanisms apply to problematic gaming. This scoping review examined literature on the relationship between PTSD, trauma, and gaming. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, Medline, CINAHL, Communication & Mass Media Complete, and PsycInfo. Seventy-two studies met inclusion criteria. Five themes emerged: trauma exposure is associated with problematic gaming behaviours, gaming is used as a coping strategy, multiple mechanisms shape the trauma-gaming relationship, games and virtual reality may support trauma-focused interventions, and the literature remains mixed due to heterogeneity in definitions of trauma, measures, participant samples, and study designs. Findings indicate a predominantly positive association between trauma-related symptoms and gaming-related behaviours. Gaming was frequently described as a coping strategy in the context of trauma, although some studies did not support coping-motivated play. Studies evaluating game-based or virtual reality interventions for trauma commonly reported benefit for at least some trauma-related outcomes, while others found unclear effects or no advantage over comparison conditions. Existing research underscores a complex interplay between trauma, psychological processes, and gaming behaviours, with gaming producing highly variable functional and psychological outcomes depending on motives, emotion regulation, and individual vulnerability. Furthermore, mechanisms linking childhood trauma, PTSD, and problematic gaming remain insufficiently understood.

title: Exercise-based interventions for internet gaming disorder: current evidence, mechanistic rationale, and the augmenting role of serious games and digital therapeutics
abstract:
Background 
                     Internet gaming disorder (IGD) is an emerging public health concern among adolescents and young adults and is associated with adverse mental health, cognitive, academic and social outcomes. Exercise-based interventions may reduce IGD symptoms, but long-term adherence remains challenging. Emerging digital health technologies, including serious games, digital therapeutics, wearable devices, artificial intelligence (AI) and neuromodulation, may improve engagement, personalisation and behavioral change. 
                   
                   
                     Objective 
                     This narrative review synthesises current evidence on exercise-based interventions for IGD and examines the complementary roles of serious games, digital therapeutics, wearable technologies, AI-assisted personalisation and neuromodulation in treatment engagement, adherence, assessment and monitoring. It also identifies evidence gaps and priorities for future research. 
                   
                   
                     Methods 
                     A narrative review was performed based on literature identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science up to March 2026, with relevant later publications also considered. We synthesised evidence regarding exercise interventions and emerging digital health technologies for the prevention and management of IGD. 
                   
                   
                     Results 
                     Exercise-based interventions may reduce IGD symptoms and improve executive function and emotional regulation, although findings vary across modalities and protocols. Serious games and exergaming may enhance motivation and adherence, while digital therapeutics such as virtual reality-based interventions remain supported by limited clinical evidence. Neuromodulation, particularly transcranial direct current stimulation, may improve inhibitory control, although effects on craving are inconsistent and no trial has combined tDCS with exercise in IGD. Wearable and AI-assisted approaches have mainly been studied for IGD assessment, classification and behavioral monitoring, with no direct evidence of clinical outcome benefits. Adaptive intervention delivery has been demonstrated mainly in non-IGD digital health settings. Safety data are limited because adverse events were not consistently assessed or reported. Overall, evidence remains constrained by heterogeneous designs, small samples, inconsistent outcomes and limited long-term follow-up. 
                   
                   
                     Conclusion 
                     Combining exercise with digital health technologies is a conceptually promising but not yet empirically validated approach to improve IGD management. Future research should prioritise high-quality multicentre randomised controlled trials, standardised outcomes, long-term follow-up, mechanistic validation, real-world implementation and ethical considerations for AI-enabled interventions in adolescents.

title: Choroid plexus volume as a marker of chronotherapeutic responsiveness in major depressive disorder
abstract: Circadian rhythm disruption is a core feature of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD). The choroid plexus (ChP), a circadian-regulated structure involved in cerebrospinal fluid production and immune signalling, has been previously associated with depression and may undergo structural changes in response to chronotherapeutics. The study included 25 patients with MDD and 25 matched healthy controls who underwent MRI. Patients received total sleep deprivation plus light therapy (TSD + LT), consisting of three 36-hour sleep deprivation cycles, each separated by a night of recovery sleep. LT was administered for 30 min every morning. Depressive symptoms, sleep quality, and chronotype were assessed through Beck's Depression Inventory (BDI), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ), respectively. ChP volumes were extracted with FreeSurfer and normalized for intracranial volume. Effects of chronotherapeutics were assessed on BDI, PSQI, and ChP volumes, with treatment response as a between-subject factor. The efficacy of treatment was also investigated stratifying for chronotype. Also, group differences in ChP volume and associations with sleep and BDI scores were explored. TSD + LT reduced depressive symptoms and improved sleep quality, with changes in PSQI associated with symptom improvement. Eveningness predicted greater depressive symptom reduction. At baseline, responders already exhibited larger left ChP volume than controls. Following treatment, a treatment × response interaction emerged for right ChP volume, showing a significant reduction in responders. Finally, reductions in both right and left ChP volumes predicted clinical improvement, and sleep quality improvement predicted right ChP volume reduction. This is the first study showing that chronotherapy modulates ChP structure in MDD, suggesting a link between circadian dysregulation and ChP enlargement proportional to clinical improvement and predicted by sleep amelioration. ChP volume may represent a biomarker of treatment responsiveness and circadian realignment.

title: IL-17 aggravates the neuroinflammatory response in depression by regulating microglial polarization through the JAK1/STAT3 signaling pathway
abstract: Background: Microglia-mediated neuroinflammation is closely related to the development of depression. As a proinflammatory cytokine, IL-17 plays a key role in various neuroinflammatory diseases. This study aimed to investigate the potential molecular mechanisms through which IL-17 affects neuroinflammation in depression through the regulation of microglial polarization. Methods: A chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced mouse model of depression and an LPS-treated BV2 cell model were used. The depression-like behavior of the mice was evaluated using the sucrose preference test (SPT), tail suspension test (TST), and forced swim test (FST). Neuronal injury was assessed using HE staining. The levels of neurotransmitters and inflammatory cytokines were analyzed using ELISA. Microglial polarization was analyzed by flow cytometry and immunofluorescence, and the expression of IL-17A and JAK1/STAT3 pathway-related proteins was assessed using Western blotting. Results: IL-17 was highly expressed in clinical specimens from patients with depression, mice treated with CUMS and BV2 cells. The inhibition of IL-17 improved depression-like behavior in CUMS-treated mice, reduced neuronal damage, and increased the expression of the neurotransmitters 5-HT, NE, and DA. In addition, IL-17 inhibition inhibited M1 microglial polarization and inflammation. In terms of molecular mechanisms, IL-17 promoted microglial M1 polarization by activating the JAK1/STAT3 signaling pathway and aggravating neuroinflammation related to depression. The use of the JAK/STAT pathway activator RO8191 attenuated the inhibitory effect of IL-17 inhibition on microglial M1 polarization. Conclusion: IL-17 activates JAK1/STAT3 signaling, promotes M1 microglial polarization, and aggravates neuroinflammation related to depression.

title: Learning-associated flexibility of cortical taste coding is impaired in Shank3 knockout mice
abstract: The ability to update the valence of sensory perception to influence behavior is crucial for survival. A common phenotype in autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) is defects in sensory processing, but whether these defects impair flexible sensory encoding is largely unexplored. In particular, how genetic risk factors such as Shank3 deletion affect the adaptability of cortical taste processing and downstream behavior is unknown. To address this gap, we performed two-photon calcium imaging during a conditioned taste aversion (CTA) learning paradigm, an ethologically relevant form of associative learning that depends on taste processing in the gustatory cortex (GC), to examine how Shank3 knockout alters taste-related neuronal activity in GC and influences CTA learning. We found that GC neurons in Shank3 knockout mice exhibited reduced stimulus-evoked suppression and increased trial-to-trial correlated variability during the acquisition of CTA memory. These activity changes, which likely reduced signal-to-noise ratio in GC, were associated with slower CTA acquisition in Shank3 knockout mice. In both genotypes, CTA learning enhanced, while subsequent extinction reduced, taste discriminability in GC, and both extinction and the associated reduction in discriminability were faster in Shank3 knockout than in wild-type mice. Together, these results show that Shank3 loss is associated with destabilized cortical activity dynamics in GC, which may contribute to inefficient encoding and maintenance of learned taste aversion. These findings show that loss of Shank3 compromises the ability of animals to update behavior to incorporate negative outcomes, and suggest this loss of flexibility may be an important feature of monogenic ASDs.

title: Taste testing: gustometry deciphered - a scoping review
journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
abstract: To map and synthesize the protocols and methodological approaches used in chemical gustometry with taste solutions, focusing on taste assessment methods, the solutions and substances employed, concentration ranges and units of measurement, and the procedures used to determine taste thresholds. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently and in duplicate by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. The review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and was prospectively registered on the Open Science Framework. Of 6,881 records identified, 10 studies met the eligibility criteria, comprising 722 participants across three clinical contexts (oncology/hematology, diabetes mellitus, and otologic disease). The whole-mouth sip-and-spit method and assessment of detection/recognition thresholds were most frequently used. Substantial heterogeneity in methods, tastants, and concentration units limited comparability across studies. Standardization of chemical gustometry protocols remains a challenge given the methodological heterogeneity identified, underscoring the need for greater methodological rigor and consistency in future research to improve reproducibility and cross-study comparability.

title: From Composition to Perception: Venus Flytrap Domain Biosensors of the Human Sweet Taste Receptor for Quantifying Sweetness
abstract: Sweetness is still judged by sensory panels throughout food manufacturing, because no validated function maps composition onto sweetness: relative sweetness varies with reference concentration, sweetener interactions change with the matrix, and composition and perception diverge even in unblended raw materials. Instrumental methods all return composition or a bulk property, and lipid-membrane taste sensors recognize solute charge rather than sweetness. This review examines the Venus flytrap (VFT) domain of the human sweet taste receptor as the recognition element for closing that gap. It maps sweet ligands onto primary and secondary binding sites, which fixes the sweeteners a construct can cover; compares routes based on cells, membrane-mimetic carriers and isolated domains; and finds performance reporting concentrated on limits of detection far below use levels. Most isolated-domain engineering has used the umami receptor T1R1, whose immobilization chemistry, protection strategies and multi-week stability have not been tested on TAS1R2-VFT. Two TAS1R2-VFT transducers have been reported, and no receptor-based method has yet been calibrated or validated against a sucrose equivalent scale. Calibration to sucrose equivalent concentration, constructs covering more than one domain, formulations not requiring ultra-low-temperature storage, and attribution of responses in real matrices remain the tasks.

title: From Taste Perception to Metabolic Regulation: Associations Among Taste Sensitivity, Taste- and Metabolic Trait-Related Genes, Body Composition and Lipid Mediator Signaling in a Human Explanatory Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Taste sensitivity has been associated with body mass index (BMI) independently of dietary intake, suggesting that taste-related pathways may influence metabolic health beyond food consumption. However, the mechanisms underlying these associations remain unclear. We investigated relationships among taste-related and metabolically relevant single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), body composition, red blood cell (RBC) total lipids, fatty acids (FAs), and lipid mediators to identify potential associations between taste perception and metabolic phenotype. Methods: Body composition, RBC total lipids, FAs, and N-acylethanolamines (NAEs) were assessed in 52 healthy subjects genotyped for selected SNPs in taste-related genes (TAS1R2, TAS1R3, GNAT3, CD36), and genes involved in nutrient-sensing NAE metabolism (FGF21, FAAH and PPARα). The associations were evaluated using explanatory univariate analyses and regression models. Results: Carriers of the GNAT3 rs7792845 CC genotype showed a lower mean fat-free mass percentage and higher RBC total lipids than carriers of the CT genotype. CD36 rs1761667 and rs1984112 were associated with NAE lipid mediators and rs1761667 with RBC total lipids, with AA genotype carriers showing higher mean values. Regression analyses identified GNAT3 rs7792845, FGF21 rs838133, and taste-sensitivity scores associated with body composition, accounting for 41.5% of the variance, and CD36 rs1761667 and rs1984112 associated with lipid and NAE values, accounting for up to 38.1% of the variance. FAAH rs324420 and TAS1R2 rs35874116 were involved in RBG lipid and NAE models. The specific lipid species underlying these associations remain unknown. Conclusions: These findings suggest that sensory- and nutrient-sensing pathways might contribute to interindividual variability in metabolic phenotypes.

abstract:
Abstract 
                   Sweet-protein engineering is constrained by low-throughput functional assays. We developed VenusSweet, a deep learning-initiated workflow combining ProtSSN zero-shot prioritization, supervised LinearSVC ranking, and sweet-taste receptor assays. Four design-build-test-learn rounds evaluated 170 brazzein variants and identified VenusBraz. Across three matched experiments, VenusBraz showed a mean 36.9-fold increase in receptor-activation potency over wild type. It also outperformed H31R/E36D/E41A in side-by-side assays. A separate double-blind evaluation with 15 participants supported greater perceived sweetness; the receptor-derived fold change is not a sensory sweetness ratio. VenusBraz retained receptor activity after thermal treatment and storage for 30 days under acidic or alkaline conditions. No significant protein × pH interaction was detected in two end point experiments. Molecular dynamics suggested altered receptor-associated conformational sampling. VenusBraz warrants further formulation and safety evaluation.

title: Genetic Susceptibility, Neurodevelopmental Abnormalities, and Neuroimmune Interactions Across Major Psychiatric Disorders
abstract: Major psychiatric disorders, including schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, and autism spectrum disorder, share overlapping genetic, neurodevelopmental, and neuroimmune underpinnings that challenge traditional diagnostic boundaries. This review synthesizes evidence across three interconnected domains: convergent genetic risk affecting synaptic and immune pathways, neurodevelopmental vulnerabilities shaped by early-life insults, and neuroimmune crosstalk involving blood-brain barrier dysfunction, sustained inflammation, and complement-mediated pathology. We propose a multidimensional developmental-immune framework in which genetic liability, environmental exposure timing, and peripheral immune status jointly shape transdiagnostic trajectories. This framework reframes psychiatric disorders as dynamic interactions among stable trait-like susceptibilities and fluctuating biological states, offering a roadmap for biomarker-driven stratification and early immune-targeted interventions.

title: Vagus-Hepatic-Creatine axis modulates manic-like behaviors via hippocampal MMP19 upregulation in bipolar disorder
abstract: Bipolar disorder (BD) is associated with pronounced alterations in peripheral creatine kinase levels; however, the mechanistic basis of this phenomenon remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we conducted a translational study combining clinical assessments in 55 patients with major depressive disorder, 57 BD patients, and 55 healthy controls, alongside sleep deprivation-induced manic-like mouse models. Our findings revealed significantly elevated peripheral creatine concentrations in both BD patients and model mice, which correlated with increased hepatic expression of guanidinoacetate N-methyltransferase (GAMT), a rate-limiting enzyme in creatine biosynthesis. Behavioral experiments in mice showed that exogenous creatine supplementation recapitulated manic-like phenotypes, whereas administration of the creatine analogue β-guanidinopropionic acid (β-GPA) or surgical subdiaphragmatic vagotomy effectively ameliorated these aberrant behaviors. Mechanistically, peripherally derived creatine was found to modulate neural activity independently of blood-brain barrier penetration, acting instead through interleukin-1α (IL-1α)-mediated inflammatory signaling. Transcriptomic analyses further identified hippocampal matrix metalloproteinase-19 (MMP19) as a critical downstream effector, and genetic knockdown experiments confirmed its indispensability in the expression of manic-like behaviors. Collectively, these results delineate a previously unrecognized vagus-liver-creatine-hippocampal axis in BD pathophysiology, highlighting peripheral creatine metabolic routes as actionable targets for therapeutic intervention. Overall, this work provides compelling evidence that peripheral metabolic disturbances can drive central nervous system dysfunction via neuroimmune crosstalk, offering a new conceptual framework for understanding mood disorder etiology.

title: Stem cell therapy attenuates cerebellar histological alterations and blood-brain barrier disruption in experimental fibromyalgia: involvement of mast cells, autophagy, and NLRP3/IL-1β neuroinflammatory pathway
abstract: Fibromyalgia is a prevalent and debilitating condition that results in generalized musculoskeletal pain, trouble sleeping, exhaustion, psychological challenges, and social problems. As a consequence of fibromyalgia's substantial therapeutic and socioeconomic burden caused by its high prevalence, uncertain etiology, wide spectrum of clinical manifestations, and sophisticated therapy, a considerable interest has emerged in investigating novel aspects of its pathophysiology, particularly those related to anxiety, depression, and cerebellar histological alterations. Such investigations may contribute to the development of effective therapeutic strategies, including the use of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) as a promising treatment approach. Rats were randomly divided into three groups: control, fibromyalgia and fibromyalgia-stem cell groups. Behavioral assessment was carried out. Cerebellar cortices were collected for histological, immunohistochemical, and morphometric analysis. Fibromyalgia group revealed anxiety-like behavioral changes, and neurodegenerative changes with blood-brain barrier (BBB) affection. Furthermore, NLRP3 and IL-1β immune-expression were significantly increased, with significant increase in the total number of mast cells with marked degranulation. Additionally, there was a significant decrease in Calbindin D-28k (CB), Beclin-1 and LC3 immune-expression. Fibromyalgia-stem cells group revealed amelioration in behavioral alterations, histological improvement, significant decrease in CD117, NLRP3 and IL-1β immune-expression, besides a significant increase in CB, Beclin-1 and LC3 immune-expression. This study represents one of the first experimental studies investigating the potential therapeutic value of BMSCs therapy in fibromyalgia-related cerebellar damage through neuroprotective mechanisms involving enhancement of autophagy, mast cell deactivation, and suppression of NLRP3/IL-1β mediated neuroinflammation with improvement of BBB structural integrity.

title: Neuromelanin-inspired metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks restore neuronal excitability in radiation-induced brain injury
abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) affects up to 30% of patients receiving cranial radiotherapy, representing an irreversible complication lacking effective therapies. Research advances are limited by poor blood-brain barrier drug penetration and overreliance on ex vivo pathology, which cannot resolve dynamic neuronal dysfunction. Inspired by neuromelanin, we fabricated metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks (MSMNs), combined with in vivo electrophysiology to investigate and mitigate radiation-triggered neural dysfunction. In 6-gray whole body-irradiated mice, MSMN normalized neuronal excitability and restored medium spiny neuron firing and striatal circuit activity, improving locomotor and anxiety-related behaviors. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. This work identifies neuronal excitability as an underexplored therapeutic target for RIBI, establishing neuromelanin-mimetic selenomelanin nanonetworks as a bioinspired platform linking molecular radioprotection to circuit-level restoration for radiation-induced neurological injury.

title: Are we moving forward from amisulpride? LB-102 (N-methyl amisulpride) in acute schizophrenia
abstract: Schizophrenia has a low prevalence but a high health burden. Although used in schizophrenia, amisulpride has limited blood-brain barrier penetration. LB-102 (N-methylated amisulpride) maintains the ability to antagonize D2- and 5-HT7-receptors with longer receptor occupancies than amisulpride. A phase 2 clinical trial (NOVA) has showed that LB-102 has some efficacy in acute schizophrenia, but this comes with adverse events, such as increased prolactin levels, that need further investigation. The inpatient setting of NOVA may have contributed to the improvement observed with LB-102. Based on NOVA, LB Pharmaceutics have moved LB-102 into phase 3 for the treatment of acute exacerbations of schizophrenia. Like NOVA, the participants of NOVA2 will be inpatients. Consequently, this trial will not address the issue of whether LB-102 is effective in the outpatient setting, and these needs testing. A recently approved new approach to treating schizophrenia is the bitopic M1/M4 muscarinic receptor agonist xanomeline. When xanomeline was compared to amisulpride, it ranked lower. In conclusion, further clinical trials are needed to determine whether LB-102 is better than amisulpride and xanomeline in the treatment of schizophrenia in both inpatients and outpatients.

title: Assessment of glymphatic function in children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and its presentations
abstract: Although attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) exhibited impairments in the glymphatic system of the brain, changes in the glymphatic system in the clinical presentations of ADHD remain unknown. This study aimed to use multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to assess the function of the glymphatic system in ADHD and its presentations. T1 structural MRI and functional MRI data from 137 neurotypical controls (NCs) and 119 patients with ADHD were collected from the ADHD200 dataset, including 61 cases of ADHD-combined type, 5 cases of ADHD-hyperactive/impulsive type, and 53 cases of ADHD-inattentive type. To assess glymphatic function, choroid plexus (CP) volume and coupling of blood-oxygen-level-dependent signals and cerebrospinal fluid signals (BOLD-CSF) were calculated. A general linear model was used for group comparisons between NC and ADHD, as well as among NC and different ADHD presentations, controlling for age, sex, site effects and head motion. Correlation analysis was performed to elucidate the relationships between glymphatic functional indicators and clinical scales. Compared to NCs, no significant differences in CP volume and BOLD-CSF coupling were observed between the overall ADHD group and NC. However, BOLD-CSF coupling was significantly enhanced in the ADHD-inattentive group (all p ≤ 0.004). Additionally, negative trends were found between BOLD-CSF coupling and full scale IQ-2 subtest score for ADHD-inattentive group (r = -0.68 ∼ -0.51). ADHD-inattentive patients demonstrated increases in BOLD-CSF coupling, suggesting that ADHD-inattentive may involve a different brain waste clearance pattern compared to other ADHD presentations.

title: Reduced hypoxanthine Ameliorates LPS-triggered autism-like stereotyped behaviors in intestinal Tlr4 knockout mice via the DRN ROS-5-HT axis
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) involves social deficits and severe stereotyped behavior. While central serotonin (5-HT) systems and Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) activation are known to be implicated in ASD, how gut TLR4 affects central 5-HT and stereotyped behavior remains unknown. This study demonstrated that prenatal lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced social deficits in offspring of both intestinal Tlr4 knockout (Tlr4△IEC) and Tlr4fl/fl mice. However, the stereotyped behaviors and the inhibition of dorsal raphe nuclei (DRN) 5-HT were reduced in Tlr4△IEC-LPS mice compared with those in Tlr4fl/fl-LPS mice. By intersecting metabolites present in both colonic and cerebrospinal fluid, and selecting those exclusively changing in the colon of Tlr4fl/floffspring, hypoxanthine was identified as a metabolite that can cross the blood-brain barrier and mediate the effects of intestinal Tlr4 knockout on DRN 5-HT signaling. Remarkably, hypoxanthine and xanthine oxidase were increased in the serum of ASD children compared to typical development (TD) children. In vivo and in vitro experiments confirmed that hypoxanthine increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) and reduced 5-HT production, thereby promoting 5-HT neuron apoptosis. The inhibition of both the PI3K/AKT and 5-HT pathways in H2O2-treated PC12 cells was rescued by glutathione pretreatment in vitro. Meanwhile, the above LPS-induced DRN changes were significantly different in the Tlr4fl/fl offspring, and were reversed in the Tlr4△IEC mice after LPS exposure. Collectively, intestinal Tlr4 knockout reduces LPS-induced stereotyped behaviors, and the mechanism involves reduced hypoxanthine production and ROS-mediated inhibition of PI3K/AKT signaling, thereby decreasing 5-HT neuronal apoptosis by elevating the 5-HT level in DRN.

title: (1)H MRS reveals impact of early adversity and age on neurometabolic profiles in women
abstract: Exposure to early-life stress (ELS), including neglect or abuse, is known for its detrimental effects on brain health. This study investigated how ELS interacts with chronological age to impact on brain metabolism in middle-aged women using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H MRS) at 3 T. High-quality spectra from the hippocampus (HC) and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) from 75 women, including 53% with ELS exposure before puberty, were analyzed. Generalized additive models assessed non-linear effects of ELS severity and chronological age on neurometabolites related to neuroinflammation and neurotransmitter cycling. Significant interactions emerged for myo-inositol (Ins) in both regions and glutamine (Gln) in the PCC, where greater ELS severity was linked to age-related increases in Ins and Gln concentrations. These results were robust when additionally controlling for symptoms of depression, anxiety, and PTSD, as well as SES, education, menopause status, and smoking. The observed patterns suggest that ELS exposure before puberty, at the older age range, is associated with glial and glutamatergic alterations that are indicative of neuroinflammation, potentially reflecting vulnerability to adverse brain health outcomes.

title: Beyond monoamines: a multi-systems molecular framework for major depressive disorder
abstract: For over five decades, the monoamine hypothesis has anchored the conceptual and pharmacological approach to major depressive disorder (MDD), yet nearly one-third of patients fail to achieve remission with standard antidepressants, and therapeutic response is delayed by weeks. This narrative review offers a critical synthesis of recent high-impact literature drawn on evidence from genomic, molecular, and translational studies across six domains: genomic architecture, epigenetic dysregulation, neuroinflammation, neurotrophic signalling, gut-brain axis, and rapid-acting antidepressant mechanisms, to construct a multi-systems framework of MDD pathophysiology and, as a secondary and explicitly scoped aim, to identify translational priorities for South Asian, particularly Indian, populations; the evidence reviewed is global in scope. A 2025 genome-wide association study (GWAS) of 688,808 cases identified 697 independent associations mapping to 635 genomic risk loci implicating glutamatergic, GABAergic, and neuropeptidergic systems. Environmental stressors converge on this genetic susceptibility through DNA methylation, histone modification, and non-coding RNA-mediated epigenetic reprogramming. An inflammatory MDD subgroup, characterised by kynurenine pathway disruption and microglial dysregulation, is of interest for patient stratification. Rapid-acting antidepressants proposed to act through TrkB-BDNF-dependent synaptic plasticity offer a mechanistic account of their fast onset, although the direct-binding theory awaits independent replication. Gut microbiome dysbiosis, particularly among neurotransmitter-producing taxa, further extends the pathophysiological map beyond the brain itself. Together, these findings support a shift from a unidimensional monoaminergic model to an integrated, multi-systems molecular framework of MDD. Realising the clinical potential of this framework will require validated precision biomarker panels, dedicated South Asian GWAS cohorts, and longitudinal multi-omics studies.

title: Polysaccharides in the treatment of brain injury-related diseases: blood–brain barrier limitations and peripheral action pathways
abstract: Natural polysaccharides possess outstanding advantages including low toxicity, favorable biocompatibility, and multi-target regulatory capabilities. They hold broad application prospects in neuroprotective research on Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and depression. Owing to their high molecular weight and strong hydrophilicity, intact polysaccharides cannot readily cross the blood–brain barrier (BBB). Only a minor proportion enters the systemic circulation after oral administration. However, even under conditions of extremely low intracerebral exposure, polysaccharides still exhibit significant central neuroprotective effects. The underlying mechanism is that intact polysaccharides primarily act as fermentation substrates for gut microbiota, which then promote the production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and modulate tryptophan and bile acid metabolism. These peripheral metabolites, upon entering the circulation, further regulate peripheral immune responses and the activity of the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis, improve neurotrophic signaling and redox homeostasis, and transmit signals to resident immune cells within the central nervous system via central boundary structures. Therefore, natural polysaccharides do not directly enter the brain. Instead, they exert neuroprotective effects via a cascade pathway involving the gut microbiota-peripheral metabolites-immune and humoral network. This article systematically elaborates on its multi-pathway mechanisms of action and summarizes adjunctive brain-targeted delivery approaches, including pathology-dependent modulation of BBB permeability and brain-targeted delivery. Future research should further elucidate the causal relationships among various signaling pathways, strengthen quality control and clinical trials, and facilitate their translational application.

title: Formalizing consciousness: a comparative mathematical analysis of leading theories
abstract: This article provides a unified and accessible exposition of major mathematically articulated frameworks for consciousness: Integrated Information Theory (IIT), Global Workspace Theory (GWT), Active Inference (AIF), higher-order representation (HOR) approaches, and the Projective Consciousness Model (PCM). Building on probability theory, information theory, and geometric structures, we reformulate their core mechanisms in a shared mathematical language at the computational and algorithmic levels, following Marr's hierarchy. This enables rigorous comparison across theories that are often treated as conceptually incommensurable. Our analysis identifies shared formal tools, differences in explanatory scope, and specific questions for computational comparison. GWT emphasizes global availability; IIT emphasizes irreducible causal integration; Active Inference and HOR emphasize hierarchical inference and conscious access under uncertainty; PCM emphasizes the perspectival geometry of conscious experience. We assess computational tractability across frameworks and show that some apparent disagreements reflect differences in explanatory level rather than direct theoretical contradiction. We use this unified formal treatment to outline a route toward future computational comparisons: common testbed models in which integration, broadcasting, higher-order access, and perspectival transformations can be studied within the same agent architecture. The goal is to make overlaps, divergences, and empirical commitments across theories more explicit, thereby supporting more systematic model comparison in consciousness science.

title: Protocol for measuring the effects of cortical scotoma on visual space perception
abstract: We aim to investigate the spatial experience of patients with chronic scotomas caused by lesion to early visual cortex, including primary visual cortex (V1) and adjacent extrastriate visual areas. These experiments are conducted as part of an adversarial collaboration testing contrasting theories of consciousness: Integrated Information Theory (IIT) and two Predictive Processing accounts, Active Inference (AI) and Neurorepresentationalism (NREP). The central question is whether lesions to early visual cortex alter the experienced extent of visual space itself, or instead primarily disrupt stimulus content within an otherwise preserved visual space. To address this, we use paradigms in which patients estimate distances or spatial extents that either span a scotomatous region or fall entirely within intact visual field locations. Psychometric functions relating perceived and physical extent are modeled to estimate shifts in the point of subjective equality (PSE). According to IIT, lesions to early visual cortex, including V1 and occipital extrastriate cortex, should lead to systematic reductions in perceived spatial extent across the scotoma (negative PSE shifts), reflecting a contraction of experienced space. In contrast, Predictive Processing accounts posit that higher-level predictive mechanisms preserve spatial structure despite loss of early input, predicting little or no systematic contraction (with NREP allowing limited context-dependent effects). By quantifying distortions in perceived spatial extent, this protocol aims to distinguish between these competing theoretical predictions.

title: Semantic Processing in Unresponsive Patients With Acute Brain Injury
abstract: Early prognostication after acute brain injury (ABI) is challenging because behavioral responsiveness may not accurately reflect preserved cognitive function. Neural responses to semantic incongruity can identify language processing despite the absence of overt behavior. We investigated whether bedside EEG could detect semantic processing in unresponsive patients with ABI and whether its presence was associated with long-term outcomes. In this prospective 2-center cohort study, unresponsive adults with ABI admitted to neurologic intensive care units between 2022 and 2025 underwent bedside EEG during a language paradigm comparing congruent and incongruent sentence endings (e.g., "my favorite color is green/soon"). Semantic processing was defined by differential event-related responses within centroparietal channels (300-500 milliseconds) using cluster-based permutation testing with false discovery rate correction. Outcomes were assessed for recovery of consciousness and functional recovery (Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended score ≥4) at 12 months by blinded interviewers. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, accuracy, and likelihood ratios. Among 105 patients (mean age 58 ± 19 years; 21% women; 53% Hispanic/Latino), the most common etiologies were intracerebral hemorrhage (45%), traumatic brain injury (43%), and subarachnoid hemorrhage (10%). Withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy occurred in 31%. Semantic processing was detected in 13 patients (12%). Recovery of consciousness occurred in 77% of patients with semantic processing compared with 49% without semantic processing (odds ratio [OR] 3.5; 95% CI 0.9-13.5, p = 0.08). Functional recovery occurred in 42% with semantic processing compared with 14% without semantic processing (OR 4.5; 95% CI 1.2-16.6, p = 0.03). Semantic processing was highly specific but insensitive for predicting both recovery of consciousness (specificity 94%, sensitivity 18%) and functional recovery (specificity 92%, sensitivity 29%). After excluding patients who underwent withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy or died of non-neurologic medical complications, specificity increased to 100% for recovery of consciousness and 95% for functional recovery. EEG evidence of semantic processing can be detected in a subset of unresponsive patients with ABI during the acute phase of injury and is associated with favorable long-term outcomes. Semantic processing was a specific but insensitive biomarker of recovery, suggesting potential utility as a rule-in marker of preserved cognitive function. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger multicenter cohorts before clinical implementation.

title: ID-SCAN: a functional MRI protocol for neurophenomenological phenotyping of dissociative identity disorder without trauma provocation
abstract: Background: Dissociative identity disorder (DID) is a trauma-related dissociative disorder in which two or more identity-agents recur within one person, each experiencing and evaluating itself and its surroundings. Most existing neuroimaging paradigms rely on symptom provocation using trauma-related autobiographical material. Identity-agent effects that are independent of symptom provocation need to be disentangled from emotional responses to trauma-related material and from the co-consciousness of other identity-agents.Objective: To introduce ID-SCAN (Identity-agent State Characterisation and Analysis), a functional MRI protocol without trauma provocation for within-person neurophenomenological characterisation of identity-agent expression and switching, and to test its feasibility in a co-conscious case.Method: A woman with DID living with persistent co-consciousness between two identity-agents (Adu and Ado) completed two fMRI tasks: identity-cued evaluation of identical insect photographs the agents made sense of in opposite ways, and trait judgments about self, the other agent and a shared intimate other. Within-person analyses combined Bayesian general linear modelling, generalised psychophysiological interaction, representational similarity analysis and a pooled identity-cue switching analysis, with cross-task overlap providing a task-general baseline.Results: Adu and Ado made sense of the same insect photographs differently. Ado showed greater activation in striato-thalamic regions, whereas Adu showed greater activation in the amygdala and in the orbitofrontal and medial prefrontal cortex; the two also differed in task-evoked connectivity. Adu-as-self and Ado-as-self occupied separable positions within self-referential regions. Cue-locked activity differed by switch direction, with greater reconfiguration when switching to the less-foregrounded Adu. Cross-task overlap localised to posterior visual and dorsal parietal cortex.Conclusions: Two co-conscious identity-agents showed distinct, convergent neurophenomeno-logical signatures of expression and switching in this single case without trauma provocation. ID-SCAN suits single-case and groupwise, simulator-controlled designs and provides a candidate framework for future longitudinal and treatment-related research whose test-retest reliability and clinical sensitivity remain to be established.

title: Resilience and vulnerability factors for post-traumatic symptoms among Israeli adults: the aftermath of 7 October events
abstract: Background: Understanding the factors that contribute to resilience and vulnerability following extreme trauma is critical for improving psychological outcomes in affected populations. While previous studies have addressed this question, they often focused on a single phase of trauma or were confounded by socioeconomic and displacement factors, leaving gaps in understanding how pre-, peri-, and post-traumatic variables jointly shape psychological outcomes.Objective: The present study investigated predictors of post-traumatic stress symptoms in the aftermath of the 7 October 2023 attacks in Israel, aiming to provide an integrated model of symptom development.Method: A total of 377 Israeli adults completed online self-report measures assessing pre-, peri-, and post-traumatic experiences, including the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5). A trauma exposure index was computed from peri-trauma variables, and two sequential linear regression models, evaluated using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV), were used to examine predictors of post-traumatic symptoms.Results: While trauma-related factors, such as physical injury and proximity to the conflict zone, predicted PCL-5 scores, they explained only 12.4% of PTSD symptom variance. In contrast, the full model, including demographic, pre-, and post-traumatic variables, explained 43% of the variance. Significant predictors included pre-trauma satisfaction with social life (associated with lower PTSD symptoms; β = -.12) and community involvement (associated with higher PTSD symptoms; β = .12), as well as post-traumatic factors associated with greater symptom severity: functional decline (β = .40), psychological treatment (β = .25), news exposure (β = .14), and lower life satisfaction (β = -.23).Conclusions: These findings underscore the limited explanatory power of objective exposure and highlight the critical role of subjective experience and post-traumatic context in shaping psychological outcomes. The study offers unique insights into trauma response in a structurally resource-rich pre-traumatic context, emphasising the need for interventions that address not only exposure but also functional and emotional recovery.

title: From Quantum Brain to Quantum Mind: The Ontological Promotion Gap in Quantum-Biological Theories of Consciousness
abstract: Quantum effects in biological systems are increasingly investigated at molecular, cellular, and neural scales, yet evidence for quantum organization in a living brain does not by itself determine the ontological status of the conscious states realized by that brain. This article distinguishes seven claims often compressed under "quantum consciousness": quantum occurrence, causal relevance, constitutive relevance, phenomenal bridging, phenomenal individuation, quantum mental status, and quantum-formal adequacy. It argues that evidence for the first three-even if decisive-does not by itself establish quantum mental status. I call this cross-level inferential discontinuity the Ontological Promotion Gap. The argument is developed in relation to current quantum-biological approaches to consciousness, including hierarchical microtubule models, nuclear-spin mechanisms, non-classical neuroimaging, dissipative quantum-brain models, autopoietic quantum constraints, and quantum-like cognition. Drawing on multilevel biological organization and contemporary neurophenomenology, the paper introduces a Phenomenal Individuation Condition: for a conscious state to be non-trivially quantum, quantum-specific structure must contribute to the organization or counterfactual differentiation of the phenomenal state itself, rather than merely occur within its biological realization. Quantum-like cognition supplies the converse dissociation: quantum formalism can characterize cognition without establishing quantum physical implementation. The resulting framework yields a Level-Specific Quantum Attribution Principle and an explicit experimental decision structure for determining what different classes of quantum-biological evidence do-and do not-license us to conclude about a quantum mind.

title: Fatal pulmonary embolism following perineal hyaluronic acid injection for vaginoplasty: a case report
abstract: A 34-year-old woman collapsed one hour after an unlicensed vaginal tightening procedure involving hyaluronic acid (HA) injection performed in a non-medical setting. Clinical manifestations emerged with sudden syncope and transient loss of consciousness, followed by rapid hemodynamic deterioration upon hospital admission. The patient succumbed approximately three hours after admission. Postmortem histological examination identified extensive basophilic foreign material occluding local vaginal veins and pulmonary arteries. Histochemical analyses (Alcian blue pH 2.5, with and without hyaluronidase digestion) identified the material as HA. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and scanning electron microscope with energy-dispersive X-ray spectrometers (SEM/EDS) chemically matched the embolus, the residual injection-site gel, and the unused product. The one-hour latency supports delayed intravascular migration after tissue dissection rather than immediate intravasation. This case underscores the potential for lethal non-thrombotic pulmonary embolism (NTPE) following aesthetic genital procedures performed outside regulated healthcare environments and highlights the essential role of comprehensive forensic investigations basing a complete evidentiary chain in determining the cause of death and characterizing the embolic material.

title: Acute Pulmonary Oedema and Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure During a Probable Autonomic Dysreflexic Episode in Chronic Cervical Spinal Cord Injury: A Case Report
abstract: Autonomic dysreflexia is a life-threatening complication affecting individuals with spinal cord injuries at or above the sixth thoracic level. While episodic hypertension is its clinical hallmark, serious cardiovascular and respiratory complications may occur. We report the case of a 67-year-old male with long-standing C5-C6 tetraplegia and established autonomic dysreflexia who was admitted with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). At approximately 01:00 on hospital day 4, after receiving approximately 3 L of maintenance intravenous fluid for poor oral intake over the preceding 72 hours, he developed sudden severe breathlessness and loss of consciousness despite a previously improving oxygen requirement. Oxygen saturation fell to 77% despite oxygen therapy, while systolic blood pressure rose from a baseline of approximately 125-130 mmHg to 167 mmHg. Physical examination revealed bilateral crackles and reduced air entry. Arterial blood gas analysis showed profound hypercapnic acidaemia (pH 7.009; partial pressure of carbon dioxide 18.5 kPa). A chest radiograph showed rapidly progressive bilateral airspace opacities consistent with pulmonary oedema. His blood pressure returned towards baseline, and following high-concentration oxygen and intravenous furosemide, his oxygen requirement subsequently decreased. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography excluded pulmonary embolism, and echocardiography showed low-normal left ventricular systolic function without a major structural or valvular abnormality. The sudden respiratory deterioration, clinically significant rise in blood pressure from baseline, rapid radiographic evolution, and subsequent improvement supported acute pulmonary oedema occurring during a probable autonomic dysreflexic episode. No discrete precipitating stimulus was confirmed, although concurrent pneumonia was considered the most likely trigger for autonomic dysreflexia. Recent intravenous fluid administration and underlying cardiac vulnerability may have lowered the threshold for pulmonary oedema. This case highlights the importance of recognising a clinically meaningful rise from baseline blood pressure when a patient with high spinal cord injury develops sudden respiratory deterioration.

title: Mind the uncertainties - a cross-sectional study on perceptions of cancer risks for factors with inconclusive or limited evidence among the Swedish general public
abstract: Identifying environmental and lifestyle factors that increase the risk of cancer is a complex scientific endeavour, with the degree of certainty regarding carcinogenicity existing along a continuum. To make informed health decisions, the general public must be well informed, both about factors that increase and decrease cancer risk. However, misconceptions can easily gain a foothold in the public consciousness. This study aimed to examine perceptions of carcinogenicity in Sweden regarding factors where the scientific evidence is inconclusive or limited, in relation to demographic strata. This cross-sectional study used a pre-existing data set with a randomly selected sample of 1520 participants (18-84 years old) recruited from a Swedish online panel. Statistical analyses utilized post-stratification weights to make the results representative for the general Swedish population. Weighted univariate tests and logistic regression models were used for examining associations between demographic groups and perceptions of carcinogenicity for twelve factors with inconclusive or limited evidence. Most participants perceived snus (76%), E-cigarettes (67.1%), food additives (63.0%), stress (50.7%), and burnt food (50.4%) as carcinogenic. Whilst no significant differences were observed regarding E-cigarettes, snus was more likely to be perceived as carcinogenic by older (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 1.01; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.00-1.02 per year older) and college/university educated (1.47; 1.09-2.00) participants, while it was less likely to be perceived as carcinogenic by males (0.66; 0.48-0.90) and high-income earners (0.62; 0.40-0.95 compared to low-income earners). Food additives were more often perceived as carcinogenic by older participants (AOR 1.02; 95% CI 1.01-1.03 per year older) and middle-income earners (1.47; 1.03-2.08 compared to low-income earners), while stress and burnt food were more likely to be perceived as carcinogenic by college/university educated (1.49; 1.15-1.91 and 1.54; 1.20-1.98, respectively) participants. A large proportion of the Swedish general public endorses several unestablished cancer risk factors as carcinogenic. The heterogeneous awareness regarding different factors observed in this study illustrates how challenging it is for individuals to navigate the complex and nuanced scientific evidence regarding cancer risk factors. This highlights the importance of clear and transparent public health messaging.

title: Aviation Medicine and Cardiovascular Assessment of Aircrew: A European Society of Cardiology-Aligned Review of Integrating International Civil Aviation Organization, European Union Aviation Safety Agency, Federal Aviation Administration, and Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation Aeromedical Standards
abstract: Aeromedical certification is based on a safety-first principle: a pilot or other aircrew member must not have a medical disorder that creates an unacceptable risk of sudden or subtle incapacitation during flight. Cardiovascular disease remains one of the most important determinants of flight fitness, as it may impair consciousness, judgment, rhythm stability, exercise capacity, and hemodynamic reserve. Modern aeromedical decision-making therefore requires the integration of aviation law, operational risk, contemporary cardiology guidelines, advanced imaging, biomarkers, and long-term surveillance. The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 1 provides the global licensing framework; the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) Part-MED, together with its Acceptable Means of Compliance and Guidance Material, defines detailed operational standards in Europe; and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) employs a protocol- and special issuance-based system for many cardiovascular and metabolic disorders. This review summarizes the aeromedical assessment of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic and acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, cardiomy-opathies, arrhythmias and conduction disorders, pacemakers and implantable cardiac devices, valvular heart disease, aortic disease, congenital heart disease, venous throm-boembolism, cardiovascular pharmacotherapy, and major respiratory conditions rel-evant to flight certification. The manuscript is aligned with current European Society of Cardiology cardiovascular guidance and with the operational aeromedical principles applied by ICAO, EASA, FAA, and the Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation. In general, preserved ventricular function, absence of significant symptoms, low thrombo-embolic and arrhythmic risk, stable treatment, and adequate exercise capacity support certification or restricted certification. In contrast, uncontrolled hypertension, unstable diabetes, significant residual myocardial ischemia, reduced ejection fraction, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, implantable defibrillator therapy, severe valvular disease, significant aortic pathology, major congenital hemodynamic lesions, or poorly controlled sleep apnea usually preclude certification. Final decisions remain individualized and depend on license class, operational role, treatment burden, surveillance data, and the judgment of the aeromedical authority.

Nitrous oxide-induced methionine synthase inhibition may precipitate transient ischaemic events in genetically susceptible patients.

title: Emotional or cognitive pathways to Internet gaming disorder symptoms? A three-wave longitudinal study
abstract: Executive function and emotion regulation are cognitive and affective facets of self-regulation that may contribute to Internet gaming disorder (IGD). However, the dynamic longitudinal associations among emotion regulation flexibility, executive function difficulties, and IGD symptoms remain unclear during adolescence and emerging adulthood. This study aimed to examine their reciprocal associations and explore whether these associations differed by gender. A three-wave longitudinal study with 3-month intervals was conducted among 1341 university students (46.5 % female, Mage = 19.31 years, SD = 0.90). Random-intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs) were used to distinguish within-person processes from stable between-person differences. Results showed that poorer emotion regulation flexibility and greater self-reported executive function difficulties were associated with more severe IGD symptoms at the between-person level. At the within-person level, emotion regulation flexibility and IGD symptoms showed bidirectional associations between T1 and T2, but not T2 and T3. Self-reported executive function difficulties positively predicted subsequent IGD symptoms during the first interval only, whereas IGD symptoms did not significantly predict later executive function difficulties. Multi-group analyses further suggested gender-specific differences, with emotion regulation flexibility and IGD symptoms bidirectionally associated from T1 to T2 in males, whereas females showed a sequential pattern in which lower emotion regulation flexibility predicted subsequent self-reported executive function difficulties, which then predicted later IGD symptoms. These findings highlight distinct emotional and cognitive pathways underlying IGD symptoms among university students. They may help guide developmentally and gender-sensitive prevention and risk-monitoring efforts targeting elevated IGD symptoms.

title: Clinical Risk Factors for Suicide in Persons With Epilepsy: A Nationwide Population-Based Case-Control Study
abstract: Individuals with epilepsy face an elevated risk of suicide, but risk factors for suicide remain incompletely understood. We conducted a nationwide case-control study in Sweden to investigate clinical characteristics associated with suicide risk in persons with epilepsy. Persons with epilepsy were identified through Swedish nationwide registers, with epilepsy diagnoses validated through medical record review. Cases were individuals who died by suicide between 2006 and 2011, validated through autopsy reports, and controls were derived from the source population using similar validation procedures. Characteristics included epilepsy type, etiology, tonic-clonic seizure (TCS) frequency, antiseizure medication (ASM) treatment, living conditions, and psychiatric comorbidity. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs were estimated using conditional logistic regression. The study included 111 suicide cases and 1,147 controls. Suicide cases had a mean age at epilepsy onset of 20 years, and 35% were female. Alcohol abuse (OR 11.81, 95% CI 6.25-22.30) and other substance abuse (OR 10.71, 95% CI 4.52-25.38) showed stronger associations than depression (OR 2.94, 95% CI 1.56-5.53) and anxiety disorders (OR 2.93, 95% CI 1.57-5.44). Living alone was associated with increased risk (OR 2.59, 95% CI 1.58-4.26). Recent TCS showed a dose-response relationship, with the highest risk among individuals experiencing 4-10 TCS in the preceding year (OR 5.01, 95% CI 2.2-11.3). Structural and unknown epilepsy etiologies were associated with elevated risk (OR 3.07, 95% CI 1.0-9.5 and OR 8.80, 95% CI 2.9-27.1, respectively). ASM treatment was associated with lower suicide risk (monotherapy OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.27-0.95; polytherapy OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.1-0.5), and nonadherence was associated with higher risk (OR 3.02, 95% CI 1.8-5.1). This study identified a distinct risk profile for suicide in persons with epilepsy, highlighting alcohol and substance abuse, living alone, seizure burden, nonadherence, and structural or unknown etiologies as key risk factors. The stronger associations for substance abuse may reflect characteristics specific to epilepsy populations and the focus on completed suicide. Screening for substance abuse and improved seizure control may contribute to suicide prevention. Major limitations include the modest number of cases and incomplete information on prior suicidal behavior.

title: Self-disgust and the body as a target in self-harm and suicidal behavior: A narrative review
journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
abstract: Self-harm and suicidal behavior are commonly framed as failures of emotion regulation, yet the emotions that make the body the target of harm remain under-specified. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on self-disgust as a candidate mechanism in non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) and in suicidal ideation and behavior. Self-disgust is an aversive self-directed emotion organized around the appraisal of the self, and often the body, as revolting or contaminated. Cross-sectional studies consistently link self-disgust with NSSI, suicidal ideation, and suicide-risk scores, and qualitative accounts place it at the center of some suicidal crises. Longitudinal studies from China suggest it mediates reciprocal links between emotional abuse and suicidal ideation and a path from body-image concerns to NSSI. Two prospective studies testing different roles did not support them, and the only induction study of self-harm urges is equivocal. In some studies, self-disgust explains variance beyond depression and constructs of the interpersonal theory of suicide. Its boundaries with shame and self-criticism are contested, and, across disorders, associations shrink when other negative self-referential emotions are controlled for. The central proposal, that the contamination-and-elimination logic of disgust explains why distress is enacted on the body, builds on earlier suggestions and remains an untested hypothesis. On this hypothesis, self-disgust is an embodied emotion whose action tendency of cleansing and removal may correspond to the phenomenology of cutting and, in some people, to a wish to eliminate a self experienced as contaminated. Implications for assessment and intervention, which remain untested, are outlined with falsifiable predictions for research.

title: Childhood trauma, post-traumatic stress disorder, and age at onset in adult separation anxiety disorder: a cross-sectional outpatient study
abstract: Adult separation anxiety disorder (ASAD) can persist from childhood or first emerge in adulthood, but the relationships of reported age at onset with childhood trauma and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) remain unclear. We compared adults with ASAD and comparison participants and examined trauma-related correlates of ASAD severity and differences between child-onset and adult-onset groups. This cross-sectional outpatient study included 120 adults with ASAD and 110 selected hospital-based comparison participants. ASAD was diagnosed using the Structured Clinical Interview for Separation Anxiety Symptoms; relevant SCID-5 components assessed traumatic experiences and PTSD. Participants completed the Adult Separation Anxiety Questionnaire (ASAQ), Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ), and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Analyses included group comparisons and hierarchical linear regression with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple testing. Adults with ASAD had higher ASAQ, CTQ, and HADS scores than comparison participants (d = 2.34, 0.63, and 0.99, respectively; all adjusted p < .001), and separation from the mother during the first year of life was more frequent (17.5% vs. 3.6%; adjusted p = .002). No onset-group comparison met the adjusted significance threshold; PTSD was recorded in 7/46 (15.2%) participants reporting adult onset and 1/74 (1.4%) reporting childhood onset (adjusted p = .055). Higher CTQ scores were associated with greater ASAQ severity after adjustment for demographic and clinical variables (B = 0.477, β = 0.358, 95% CI [0.243, 0.711]; adjusted p < .001), accounting for an additional 11.1% of the variance. The association persisted in sensitivity analyses, although model checks suggested possible nonlinearity. ASAD was associated with greater childhood trauma and affective symptom burden, and childhood trauma remained associated with separation anxiety severity after adjustment for measured covariates. The numerical PTSD pattern remains descriptive and requires replication; it does not establish distinct clinical profiles or developmental pathways.

title: PPP1R1B differentially modulates alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity through distinct prefrontal circuits
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
abstract: Excessive alcohol consumption frequently co-occurs with anxiety and depression in alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet the specific neural circuits and molecular mechanisms coordinating these comorbid conditions remain poorly defined. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), particularly its prelimbic (PL) and infralimbic (IL) subregions, projects to key reward and emotion centers like the nucleus accumbens (Nac) and basolateral amygdala (BLA), but the functional heterogeneity of these projections is unclear. Using chemogenetics, retrograde tracing, electrophysiology, spatial proteomics, and cell-type-specific gene editing in mice subjected to a 4-wk intermittent access to alcohol (IAA) paradigm, we selectively manipulated glutamatergic projections from the PL and IL to the Nac core, Nac shell, and BLA and assessed alcohol intake, anxiety-like, and depression-like behaviors. Chemogenetic activation of PL-Nac core projections reduced short-term alcohol intake, anxiety-, and depression-like behaviors, while IL-BLA activation decreased alcohol consumption and anxiety-like behaviors only. Retrograde tracing revealed mirror-image anatomical segregation of projection-defined neuronal subpopulations within PL/IL linking spatial organization to functional divergence. IAA induced pathway-specific synaptic adaptations. Spatial proteomics nominated protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a candidate molecule in PL-Nac core neurons. Independent immunostaining confirmed PPP1R1B downregulation, and circuit-specific knockout recapitulated alcohol-related and affective phenotypes, whereas overexpression reversed them. In IL-BLA neurons, PPP1R1B manipulation modulated alcohol intake and anxiety, but not depression. These findings define a subregion- and projection-specific organizational logic in the mPFC for differentially regulating alcohol consumption and emotional comorbidity, with PPP1R1B as a key molecular determinant. This provides a neural pathway-molecule framework for targeted intervention in AUD.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Behavioral Phenotyping: From Behavioral Neuroscience to Depression Research
abstract: Behavioral phenotyping remains the main experimental readout for investigating brain function and neuropsychiatric disease. However, conventional behavioral analysis relies largely on manually defined endpoints that simplify the multidimensional nature of behavior and often overlook subtle behavioral dynamics. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL) and computer vision, are fundamentally transforming this landscape by enabling automated, high-resolution quantification of behavior across species and experimental paradigms. This review discusses recent developments in AI-based behavioral phenotyping and their implications for translational neuroscience, with particular emphasis on emerging applications to depression research. We first describe how markerless pose estimation has changed movement quantification, followed by supervised and unsupervised ML approaches that classify predefined behaviors or discover latent behavioral motifs directly from movement data. We then discuss how these approaches are reshaping systems neuroscience by enabling increasingly detailed descriptions of behavioral organization and facilitating the investigation of behavior as a continuous, multidimensional process. Finally, we examine their application to experimental models and clinical studies of depression, considering their potential and the limitations of translating computational behavioral measures across experimental and clinical settings. AI-based behavioral phenotyping represents an important methodological advance in neuroscience, shifting behavioral analysis from the quantification of isolated experimental endpoints toward the characterization of integrated behavioral states. In depression research, these approaches may improve behavioral characterization in experimental models and provide quantitative measures of clinically-relevant behavioral alterations in humans. However, linking experimental and clinical phenotypes will require methodological standardization, independent validation, and careful evaluation of cross-species comparability.

title: Down-regulation of circular RNA MBNL1 inhibits monocytic activation to alleviate depressive-like behaviors in mice
abstract: Clinical studies have reported that elevated inflammatory markers are closely associated with the development of stress-related disorders, such as major depressive disorder (MDD), although the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have been reported to be associated with MDD. The present study reveals that circMBNL1 expression is significantly upregulated in both plasma and monocytes from patients with MDD and positively correlates with the severity of depressive symptoms. We demonstrate that circMBNL1 drives pro-inflammatory activation of monocytes and promotes their infiltration into the brains of mice subjected to chronic unpredictable stress (CUS), thereby exacerbating neuroinflammation. Notably, extracellular vesicle (EV)-delivered sicircMBNL1 specifically downregulates circMBNL1 expression in peripheral monocytes, thereby attenuating Ly6Chi monocyte infiltration, preserving blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, suppressing microglial activation, restoring astrocytic function, and ultimately alleviating depressive-like behaviors in mice. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that circMBNL1 knockdown induces ubiquitin-mediated degradation of the transcription factor STAT3, leading to downregulation of placental growth factor (PGF) expression and consequent suppression of monocyte activation. Our findings provide the first evidence implicating the circMBNL1-STAT3-PGF axis as a key mediator of neuroinflammatory processes in MDD, opening new avenues for developing targeted therapeutic strategies for depression.

title: Inflammatory biomarkers in late-life depression: a systematic review and meta-analysis of interleukin-1β, interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and C-reactive protein
abstract: Late-life depression (LLD)-encompassing both major depressive disorder and clinically significant depressive symptoms-affects approximately 1-5% of adults aged 60 and older when defined by strict diagnostic criteria, while clinically significant depressive symptoms affect 8-16% of community-dwelling older adults. Antidepressant treatment in older adults is challenging due to smaller effect sizes, higher treatment resistance, and greater risk of adverse effects, pointing to unique, understudied mechanisms. The inflammatory hypothesis of depression and the "inflammaging" theory together suggest that chronic peripheral and central inflammation drive LLD pathogenesis. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized data from 18 observational studies (1,593 LLD patients, 2,776 healthy controls) to evaluate peripheral levels of interleukin-1β (IL-1β), IL-6, C-reactive protein (CRP), and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α). All four markers were significantly elevated in LLD (Hedges' g = 0.52-0.80, all p < 0.01), with high between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 83-90%). Sensitivity analyses restricting to studies with adequate confounding adjustment attenuated effect sizes, particularly for CRP (57% reduction) and TNF-α (36% reduction), but all markers remained significant. Subgroup analyses identified study population, geographic region, medication status, and sample size as potential effect moderators, but these should be interpreted as study-level moderators rather than evidence for patient-level subtypes. These findings are consistent with an inflammatory contribution to LLD, though the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference and the magnitude of effect may be partially inflated by incomplete control of somatic comorbidities. Future studies should employ individual participant data meta-analyses with multi-marker profiling to test whether distinct inflammatory subtypes exist.

title: Can AI-assisted analysis of antidepressant drug online reviewers (ADORE) inform real-world use of antidepressants?
abstract: Antidepressant selection is constrained by limited comparative-effectiveness data, with randomized trials measuring symptom reduction rather than patient-reported tolerability. We tested whether AI-assisted analysis of patient-written online reviews recovers drug-level tolerability signals that converge with the strongest randomized evidence. We did a cross-sectional analysis of 8348 reviews of 16 antidepressants for major depressive disorder posted to Drugs.com (February 2008-March 2025; ≥1 month reported use). Two independent large language models (Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro) classified each review across 17 clinical dimensions using identical structured prompts; a stratified 100-review subsample (1700 classifications per reviewer) was independently rated by two experts, with all agreement statistics highly significant. We compared per-drug top-rating prevalence with Cipriani et al.'s 2018 network meta-analysis retention and efficacy odds ratios (Spearman correlation). Mean inter-LLM Cohen's κ was 0.81; expert reviewers agreed substantially with the dual-AI consensus (mean κ = 0.75 and 0.80). Top rating correlated strongly with Cipriani et al. retention odds ratios (ρ = +0.79, p < 0.001) but not with efficacy odds ratios (ρ = -0.14, p = 0.64). Within-SNRI heterogeneity was substantial. Emotional blunting was the strongest negative predictor of satisfaction (OR 0.20). Reviews are from a single platform and self-selected users; drug-level comparisons rest on few agents; and the design is cross-sectional and ecological. AI-classified patient reviews recover the drug-level tolerability signal of randomized retention data and surface within-class heterogeneity, particularly among SNRIs, as a hypothesis-generating signal. Within the comparable-efficacy range of contemporary antidepressants, tolerability, especially emotional blunting, principally correlates with patient satisfaction.
